name: NLWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Tails, from 1 February 2009; 4 reigns are recorded, the last held by Brenton Cyrus and still running when the record ends.
notes: The one-year show of 18 January 2010 bills The Notorious K.I.D as 'Heavyweight and Undisputed Champion'; which heavyweight belt that is, and when he won it, is not on the recovered pages.

name: NLWF Universal Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Havoc, from about 8 March 2009; 8 reigns are recorded, the last held by Frank Hart and still running when the record ends.
notes: Its champions page lists the same history under both brands; the shows give two belts only after 28 June 2009.

name: NLWF Universal Heavyweight Championship (Legacy, from 28 June 2009)
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Demetrius Randall, from 28 June 2009; 1 reign are recorded, the last held by Demetrius Randall and still running when the record ends.
notes: A second belt from the draw at Simple Survival, which un-unified the Undisputed Universal Championship; its history before 28 June 2009 is the Universal Heavyweight Championship's.

name: NLWF North American Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Jackson, from 1 February 2009; 7 reigns are recorded, the last held by Frank Hart and still running when the record ends.
notes: The Junior Heavyweight Championship was unified into it on 9 May 2009.

name: NLWF Junior Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Brenton Cyrus, from 1 March 2009; 4 reigns are recorded, the last held by Alex Mark, ending 9 May 2009.

name: NLWF No Limit Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Death Angel, from 10 March 2009; 4 reigns are recorded, the last held by Swan Lee and still running when the record ends.
notes: Its champions page also lists an Alex Mark reign from 06/09/09, defeating 'Frank Hart/Unified Title', with the same 22 days as his North American row; no recovered card shows it, and Simple Survival calls Swan Lee the current champion, so it is not recorded as a reign.

name: NLWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is The Heart Attacks, from 1 February 2009; 4 reigns are recorded, the last held by The Mexican Samurai and Shadow Demon and still running when the record ends.

name: NLWF Universal Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is DX Affliction, from 7 March 2009; 4 reigns are recorded, the last held by 25 to Life and still running when the record ends.
notes: The Direct Hit tag belts, called Universal Tag Team Titles and Undisputed Tag Team Titles on the pages; on Direct Hit 12 the World Tag Team Titles were unified into them.

name: NLWF Freedom Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Chuck Matthews, from 13 June 2009; 3 reigns are recorded, the last held by Kaos and still running when the record ends.

name: NLWF Annihilation Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Brenton Cyrus, from 17 April 2009; 2 reigns are recorded, the last held by Death Angel and still running when the record ends.

name: NLWF Proving Grounds Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Conor O'Sullivan, from 25 April 2009; 2 reigns are recorded, the last held by Aaron O'Shea and still running when the record ends.

name: NLWF Women's World Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Tiffany Starr, from 7 June 2009; 1 reign are recorded, the last held by Tiffany Starr and still running when the record ends.

name: NLWF Undisputed Championship
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Steven Angel; 3 reigns are recorded, the last held by Jason Hawk and still running when the record ends.

name: NLWF Undisputed Tag Team Titles
epitaph: The first champion on the recovered pages is Nick Ridicule and Chuck Matthews; 2 reigns are recorded, the last held by Ryan Apollo and still running when the record ends.
